task_production_rates.name: Inspect Ceiling Surface
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walking inspection of ceiling with raking work light. ~17% slower than wall inspection (1500 SF/hr) due to overhead viewing angle and lighting setup. QT2 uses this same task but at faster pace (~1600 SF/hr) with quick walk-through and major defects only. QT4 uses separate TSK_CEIL_INSPECT_QT4 task with comprehensive inspection.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Ceiling Surface (Premium)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Detailed ceiling inspection with raking work light. ~15% slower than wall QT4 inspection (1000 SF/hr) due to overhead angle.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum Ceiling Drywall Dust
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: HEPA vacuum overhead with extension pole. ~12% slower than wall vacuum (800 SF/hr). Less dust on ceilings but overhead reach is slower.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall Edge
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Freehand brush cut-in at wall line from ceiling perspective. ~15% slower than wall cut-in (100 LF/hr) due to overhead arm position. QT2 uses same task at faster pace (~100 LF/hr) due to relaxed precision - minor wavering acceptable if coverage complete. QT4 uses separate TSK_CEIL_CUT_IN_WALL_QT4 task with crisp edge requirement.

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall Edge (Premium)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Careful ceiling brush cut-in for crisp straight line. ~13% slower than wall QT4 cut-in (75 LF/hr) due to overhead position.

task_production_rates.name: Roll Primer on Ceiling
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Single journeyman, 9-inch roller on extension pole, overhead. ~14% slower than wall rolling (350 SF/hr) due to overhead fatigue and roller control.

task_production_rates.name: Roll Primer on Textured Ceiling
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Textured ceiling surface with 3/4-inch nap roller overhead. ~15% slower than wall textured rolling (275 SF/hr).

task_production_rates.name: Roll Primer on Ceiling (Premium)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Premium ceiling roller application. ~15% slower than wall QT4 rolling (275 SF/hr). Overhead fatigue + quality attention.

task_production_rates.name: Mask Adjacent Surfaces for Ceiling Spray
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply tape and paper to wall tops for ceiling spray masking. ~13% slower than wall masking (150 LF/hr) — working at ceiling line is overhead reach.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (Full Room)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Full room floor coverage with rosin paper or plastic. Tape seams. Larger scope than wall spray perimeter protection.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fold and remove floor protection. Faster than setup.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Primer on Ceiling
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray upward at proper mil thickness. ~17% slower than wall spray (600 SF/hr) due to overhead position, overspray management, and fatigue.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Primer on Ceiling (Premium)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Premium ceiling spray with consistent mil thickness. ~15% slower than wall QT4 spray (500 SF/hr).

task_production_rates.name: Spray Ceiling Primer (No Backroll)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray-only ceiling is faster than spray+backroll but ~18% slower than wall spray-only (700 SF/hr). Higher overlap needed overhead without backroll.

task_production_rates.name: Backroll Sprayed Ceiling Primer
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Backroll ceiling immediately after spray with 18-inch roller on extension pole. ~19% slower than wall backroll (400 SF/hr) — overhead fatigue is the dominant factor.

task_production_rates.name: Backroll Sprayed Ceiling Primer (Premium)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Premium ceiling backroll with stipple elimination. ~20% slower than wall QT4 backroll (350 SF/hr).

task_production_rates.name: Cut-In Wall Edge After Ceiling Spray
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch-up cut at wall line after removing masking. ~17% slower than wall equivalent (120 LF/hr).

task_production_rates.name: Remove Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pull tape and paper from wall tops at 45 degrees. ~8% slower than wall masking removal (300 LF/hr) — reaching overhead.

task_production_rates.name: Final Ceiling Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walking inspection of completed ceiling primer with raking light. ~12% slower than wall final inspection (2000 SF/hr).

quality_tier_effects.description: Minimal ceiling prime — reduced prep intensity, basic coverage
quality_tier_effects.notes: Economy work: quick inspection (major defects only, ambient light), coverage-priority cut-in (minor wobble acceptable), quick final inspection. Application quality is NOT reduced - drips/sags/holidays still fail. Per Modifier_Registry and Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition doctrine.

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard ceiling prime — baseline for all rates
quality_tier_effects.notes: Standard new construction: proper prep, single coat, clean edges

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium ceiling prime — thorough prep, careful application, crisp edges
quality_tier_effects.notes: Premium work: detailed inspection, straight edges, possible light sand

height_effects.notes: Baseline — work from floor with extension pole
Step ladder may be needed. Longer extension pole, more fatigue.
Scaffold or baker staging required. Significant overhead access challenge.
Scaffold or lift required. Extreme overhead work. Production rate cuts in half.

texture_effects.notes: Orange peel texture increases surface area ~15%, slows application ~15%
Knockdown texture increases surface area ~25%, slows application ~20%

drywall_level_effects.notes: Level 3 has more exposed paper, higher absorption, slightly slower application
Level 5 is uniform surface, slightly better coverage, but may require sand after prime

coupling_constraints.description: When using spray+backroll on ceilings, spray rate must not exceed backroll rate. Backroller sets the pace. Ceiling backroll rate is the bottleneck.
coupling_constraints.practical_implication: Ceiling spray at 500 SF/hr, ceiling backroll at 325 SF/hr means effective rate is 325 SF/hr per crew
coupling_constraints.notes: Spray and backroll typically done by 2-person crew. Ceiling backroll is significantly slower than wall backroll — this makes the coupling constraint even more impactful on ceilings.

crew_configurations.name: Single Ceiling Roller
crew_configurations.notes: One person does ceiling cut-in and rolling with extension pole

crew_configurations.name: Ceiling Roller Pair
crew_configurations.notes: Cutter stays ahead of roller for larger ceiling areas

crew_configurations.name: Ceiling Spray + Backroll Crew
crew_configurations.notes: Sprayer and backroller work in tandem overhead. Backroller sets pace. More fatiguing than wall spray+backroll.

crew_configurations.name: Single Ceiling Sprayer
crew_configurations.notes: Spray-only ceiling application, one person. Less common — backroll preferred for ceilings.
